operations.name: William Rutherford

expected.name: William Rutherford
expected.description: William Rutherford was an IWW member from Sacramento. William Rutherford received a four-year sentence for giving testimony in court on behalf of a fellow member of the IWW and served a prison sentence in San Quentin from August 25, 1923, to March 31, 1927. (See also the entry for J. A. Casdorf.) 1 0
expected.body: Date review: Arrested in 1922 after testifying in the Casdorf-Firey trial. The sources place the witness arrests in spring, without an individual exact day; year precision is used. This was a California criminal-syndicalism prosecution, not a federal Espionage Act case. Glendale Daily Press, June 14, 1922, page 1; People v. La Rue, 62 Cal.App. 276 (1923).

operations.source: Contemporary SanQuentin prisoner roster,Daily Worker December29,1925: https://www.marxists.org/history/usa/pubs/dailyworker/1925/1925-ny/v02b-n297-NYE-dec-29-1925-DW-LOC.pdf . Independently repeated NewLeader July18,1925: https://www.marxists.org/history/usa/pubs/new-leader/1925/v02n29-jul-18-1925-NL.pdf . SanQuentin number, not BOP register number.

operations.name: Sam Horino

expected.sentence:
Four years at the U.S. Penitentiary, Leavenworth; the convictions were reversed on appeal in 1945.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted by a federal jury in Cheyenne in October 1944 and sentenced to four years at Leavenworth; the Tenth Circuit overturned the conspiracy convictions in 1945.

Charges as recorded: Conspiracy to counsel draft evasion — for leading the Heart Mountain Fair Play Committee, which urged imprisoned Nisei to refuse induction until their constitutional rights as U.S. citizens were restored.

updates.indicted: May 10, 1944 — sealed federal grand-jury indictment, Cheyenne

operations.name: J. H. Beyer

expected.name: J. H. Beyer
expected.description:
J. H. Beyer was convicted at the mass IWW trial in Chicago and served in Leavenworth Penitentiary. Beyer jumped bail pending the appeal of his conviction and became a fugitive from the law. He is said to have taken refuge in Soviet Russia.

Before the Chicago prosecution he was one of the 74 IWW members held in the Snohomish County jail and charged with murder after the Everett Massacre of November 5, 1916, when Sheriff Donald McRae and a posse of armed vigilantes opened fire on the steamer Verona at the Everett dock, killing at least five Wobblies. The charges against all 74 were dropped after Thomas H. Tracy’s acquittal on May 5, 1917. At the time of the massacre he was 56, a painter, born in Michigan.

operations.source: EverettPublicLibrary catalog: https://epls.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/EvrtMassacre/id/60 . Name,booking number,painter occupation and Michigan birthplace match existing Everett case. Existing portrait retained. Catalog age56 conflicts with1874 birthyear; temporary erroneous release and voluntary December14 return conflict with continuous custody dates. Populated fields preserved and flagged.
